Paste a game — get it explained

Chess Coach

Paste a screenshot of a chessboard, or drop one here.

Any flat, square-on picture of a board works — this app, another app, a diagram from a book. The position is read off the picture and you get to correct it before anything is analysed.

Whose move is it?

Anything read wrong? Tap a piece, then tap the square.

Castling still allowed

Every move is explained by a chess-knowledge layer written for this app — what the move develops, what it blocks or unblocks, which pawn break it prepares, what it weakens — and then graded by Lozza, a full-strength JavaScript chess engine (MIT licensed) running offline inside this page. No engine writes prose: the engine says whether a move worked, the explanations say what it was trying to do.
Opening names come from the lichess chess-openings book (CC0), matched by position rather than move order, so a transposition is still named correctly. Everything runs on your device; nothing is uploaded.
